result:
Decision: **CONTINUE.** Round 223 is **PERF-HARNESS-SHARED-LIB**, written to `current-task.md` (decisions D-29z243…D-29z250). It is a test-only round: the helpers copied across the three perf specs move into `perf/lib/`, and nothing that is measured should change. No app code is touched.

**Round 222:** C passed it (12 rows, checked in the browser at both viewports), and it is published as `2d4a93f`, which is the baseline for round 223. The export-dialog bug (B-R220-LEGACY-EXPORT-NO-STEMS) is now marked done. C's three Low findings are ruled:
- **C-R222-01:** two WAV exports of the same mix differ by 1 LSB. I changed the check to "within 1 LSB on every sample, and the same level for every stem". The cause goes to the deferred Lows and to the export-pipeline architecture review already requested from root.
- **C-R222-02:** the Ableton manual quote was my error from the round 222 task. A new decision corrects the record; rewording doc 174 is deferred.
- **C-R222-03:** the dialog's buttons are cut off at 1280×720. This predates round 222 and is deferred.

The deferred Lows go from 345 to 351. No Critical, High or Medium finding is open.

**What round 223 asks for:**
- **New files:** `perf/lib/page.ts` and `perf/lib/report.ts`. The shared report function keeps the five real differences between the three specs as options rather than merging them. Each spec keeps its own report envelope, so the JSON stays in the same order.
- **Edits allowed in:** the three specs; one note in `perf/budgets.json`; named sections of docs 163, 168 and 169; plus new doc 175. All 1,065 other tracked files are frozen, including the other `perf/lib` files.
- **Five Low findings closed along the way:** GATE214-S2, S3 and S5, and GATE217-S1 and S2. None of them should move a measured value.
- **Split, not dropped:** the stage also asked for a stricter determinism tolerance. That would change pass/fail rules and break this round's "nothing changes" proof, so it moves with GATE214-S1/S4 and R216-MEM-POLLS-HEADROOM into a new stage, PERF-HARNESS-SHARED-LIB-b, queued right after this one.
- **Pre-ruled to avoid wasted rounds:**
  - PERF-1a already takes about half of its 15-minute timeout. A lists that; it is not a STOP.
  - Spec line references in doc sections A may not edit will go stale. They become one deferred Low.

**How C will judge it:** I re-ran all three perf specs on the baseline commit in a scratch copy. All three passed in 13.4 minutes, and those results are the reference. Every deterministic value must come out identical:

| Spec | Deterministic rows |
|---|---|
| PERF-1a | 167 |
| PERF-1b-i | 122 |
| PERF-1b-ii | 38 |

These values have not changed between earlier runs. My comparison script does catch real differences: against round 221 it flagged exactly the four JS-size rows that round 222's app change moved. C also writes its own check of the shared report code and must show it failing on three named broken versions. On top of that come the scope check, a code read, an unused-import check, the anonymous `/studio-lab` smoke test and the sign-in guard. The full test suite stays with the root gate.

**What comes next:** if C passes round 223 before 2026-10-30, round 224 is stage b. On or after that date, a regression round comes first. The next retrospective is at round 230 or at the end of this stage.

The `tech-lead` and `performance-optimizer` agents were consulted, and the advisor was used before writing and again before finishing. I followed its corrections in full. The two agents disagreed only on GATE214-S4; I kept it in stage b because it changes a liveness check. The store repository is unchanged and clean.

Other files written:
- the archived task `tasks/round-222.md` (byte-identical copy)
- `b-round-222.md`
- `b-next.json`
- `backlog.json`, version 208
- `feature-status.md`
- the hash lists
- the `b-round-222/` folder, which holds the baseline results and the comparison scripts
